[EVENT] User is thinking of scheduling a brake pad replacement for their 2015 Toyota Camry soon.  
[PREFERENCE] User is open to trying an independent shop for brake pad replacement if they are reliable.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Brake pads typically need to be replaced every 30,000 to 50,000 miles under average driving conditions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For aggressive driving or frequent city driving, brake pads may need replacement every 15,000 to 30,000 miles.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For frequent highway driving, brake pads may last 50,000 to 70,000 miles.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Signs that indicate brake pads need replacement include squealing or grinding noises, vibrations when braking, spongy brake pedal feel, low brake fluid levels, and visible wear on the brake pads.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended checking the brake pads' condition and consulting with a trusted mechanic or dealership for the best course of action.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested ways to find a reliable mechanic include checking online reviews, asking for word-of-mouth recommendations, looking for certifications, and checking local car clubs or forums.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested online resources for finding mechanics include RepairPal, MechanicNet, and AAA-Approved Auto Repair.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Average cost of replacing brake pads for a 2015 Toyota Camry is $50-$100 for OEM parts and $30-$70 for aftermarket parts per axle.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Labor costs for dealerships range from $100-$200 per axle, while independent shops range from $75-$150 per axle.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Total cost for brake pad replacement at a dealership is $200-$400, while at an independent shop it is $150-$300.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested that if the user wants OEM parts and dealership expertise, they should expect to pay a premium, while independent shops may offer savings.  
[EVENT] User is considering selling their 2007 Honda CBR600RR motorcycle.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested getting the motorcycle serviced before listing it to increase buyer confidence and potentially command a higher selling price.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided pros and cons of servicing the motorcycle before listing versus waiting for a serious buyer.
